\title{One motion solver for every MRI time series: the acquisition design inside the objective and a prior that leaves real motion alone}
\author{Brian B. Avants \\ University of Virginia}
\date{}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\section*{Synopsis}

Head-motion estimates in MRI time series absorb whatever changes the images in step with the acquisition: ASL label
alternation, diffusion contrast, eddy currents, the physiological alternation of fast BOLD. We present one solver that registers all frames of a series in a single optimisation with the acquisition
design inside its objective, applies the terms physics calls displacements, removes the terms physics calls contrast,
and damps the head trajectory with a re-descending prior gated on three phantoms with known motion and five clinical
series. On multi-shell DWI, acquisition terms hold 73 to 83\,\% of the phase-encode step and 39
to 62\,\% of the B0-immune readout step. Open software: syntx.

\section*{Introduction}

Single-reference registration assigns every design-locked image change to head motion [1,2]: ASL label alternation,
diffusion contrast and eddy currents, the physiological alternation of fast BOLD. Priors on the trajectory are the usual
remedy and carry their own risk: a prior strong enough to remove jitter removes drift and real steps with it. We present
one objective for every modality, a prior whose form lets real steps pass, and the gate that chose its weight.

\section*{Methods}

\textbf{Forward model (Figure~1A).} Frame $k$, observed at reference-space point $x$, satisfies
\begin{equation}
I_k\!\big(E_k(P_k x)\big)\,\big(1 + a_k^{\top} p\big)\,\gamma_k \;\approx\; \bar I_{\ell(k)}(x),
\qquad
P_k x = R_k (x - c) + c + t_k,
\qquad
E_k y = y + p\,\big(a_{k0} + a_k^{\top}(y - c)\big),
\label{eq:model}
\end{equation}
with $P_k$ the rigid pose about the centre $c$, $E_k$ the eddy-current affine along the phase-encode axis $p$ whose four
coefficients are linear in the diffusion gradient, $a_k = C g_k$ [3], $\gamma_k$ a per-frame gain for scanner drift and
$\bar I_{\ell(k)}$ the mean of the frame's own level (b-shell, label state, encoding state). The six pose parameters of
frame $k$ are $m_k + D_k \beta$: $m_k$ the free head pose and $D_k\beta$ the design-locked offset (per level, with the
$l = 2$ direction terms per shell), which is removed from the reported pose and never applied. One batched optimisation
over all frames maximises the Mattes mutual information of every frame against its level's reference, L-BFGS then a
coupled Newton stage; one chain per frame (rigid, then eddy affine), one interpolation.

\textbf{Prior (Figure~1B, C).} With $u_t = m_t - \tfrac12 (m_{t-1} + m_{t+1})$ the second difference of the head
trajectory in mm (rotations scaled to a 50\,mm lever arm), the objective adds
\begin{equation}
\lambda \kappa \sum_t \rho\big(|u_t|\big), \qquad
\rho(u) = \frac{\delta^2}{2}\log\!\Big(1 + \frac{u^2}{\delta^2}\Big), \qquad
\rho'(u) = \frac{u}{1 + u^2/\delta^2}, \qquad \delta = 0.05\ \text{mm},\ \lambda = 0.03,
\label{eq:prior}
\end{equation}
where $\kappa$ is the measured curvature of the image term per mm$^2$ (median over frames and translation axes at every
stage), so $\lambda$ is a fraction of the data's own curvature. The pull $\rho'(u)$ peaks at the knee $\delta$ and
re-descends: a step of a few knees is nearly free, so drift and real motion pass through while noise-level wiggles are
damped. The Newton stage uses the majoriser $\rho'(u)/u \cdot I$ for each term, since the exact Hessian is indefinite
beyond the knee. Two alternatives were gated: the Charbonnier form (quadratic below the knee) and a form with its full pull already at
$u \to 0$, the hypothesis that small second differences should be shrunk hardest.

\textbf{Gate.} A setting passes if, on three phantoms with known trajectories (ASL drift with jitter, DWI with a planted
eddy shift, slow-flow encoding states), no phantom loses more than 10\,\% FD error against no prior and DWI gains; and on
five clinical series the B0-immune readout step moves less than 0.02\,mm, alignment changes less than 1\,\% and FD
rises less than 2\,\%. Repeat runs differ by less than 0.001\,mm.

\textbf{Account.} Along each acquisition axis the frame-to-frame step variance is split into head, applied eddy and
removed design-locked shares. Per voxel, sequential sums of squares against the design, then motion regressors, then the
residual, raw and corrected. FD is computed from $m_k$ alone; for censoring, the near-Nyquist alternation is removed
from the pose series [2,4].

\textbf{Data.} Resting BOLD (TR 1.0\,s, 300 volumes), two ASL series (25 and 60 volumes), two multi-shell DWI series
($b$ = 1500/3000, 99 to 100 volumes), four cohorts, one laptop GPU. Software: syntx 6.28, antsxdwi 0.33,
antsxfunctional 0.23, antsxslowflow 2.12.

\section*{Results}

\textbf{Gate (Figure~2).} Every prior that shrinks small second differences hardest failed: at weight 0.1 the
constant-pull form raised the ASL phantom's FD error by 87\,\% and slow flow's by 55\,\%, Charbonnier by 70 and 51\,\%,
because the phantoms' sub-knee jitter is true motion. The re-descending form at 0.03 passed every gate: phantom FD error
$-14$\,\% (ASL), $-17$\,\% (DWI), $-3$\,\% (slow flow); on the five series the readout step moved at most 0.011\,mm,
alignment was unchanged, FD changed $-0.9$ to $+1.8$\,\%, and every frame converged (81 to 85\,\% without the prior, whose stage oscillates on plateau directions until
its iteration cap; BOLD 206 to 32\,s). At 0.05 the same form
lowered the high-motion DWI readout step by 0.043\,mm and was rejected.

\textbf{Account (Table~1, Figure~3).} On the two DWI series the eddy term holds 73 to 83\,\% of the phase-encode step
variance and the removed design-locked term 39 to 62\,\% of the readout step variance. After correction the design
explains 96\,\% of the voxel variance, motion after the design falls from 1.1 to 0.7\,\% and from 2.0 to 0.8\,\%, the
residual from 4.6 to 3.3\,\% and from 7.4 to 3.6\,\%, and the residual is uncorrelated with FD ($r = -0.02$, $-0.13$).
On resting BOLD, band-limited FD lowers the mean from 0.60 to 0.31\,mm and the censored fraction from 46 to 13\,\%. On
the 25-volume ASL series the levels explain 98\,\% of the variance after correction and motion after the design falls
from 0.34 to 0.18\,\%.

\section*{Discussion}

More than a third of the displacement along the axis the scanner cannot distort was design-locked, and three
quarters along phase encode was eddy: the misattribution of single-reference registration is a measured number. Our hypothesis failed: the form that removes the most sub-knee jitter on a synthetic trajectory is the one the
phantoms reject, because their jitter is real. Limitations: the phantoms plant
jitter in the trajectory, not in the images, so the claim that real sub-knee jitter is measurement noise has no phantom
gate yet; on the 60-volume ASL series the image-domain account attributes most variance to motion regressors, which we
do not interpret; censoring thresholds are not tied to a downstream outcome; a design-in-metric variant over-reports readout jitter on real DWI and is not default.

\section*{Conclusion}

One objective serves BOLD, ASL, multi-shell diffusion and slow-flow encodings; every term's share is reported with
the result; the prior is the one setting that passed phantoms with known motion and clinical data together.

\section*{References}

[1] Freire L, Mangin JF. NeuroImage 2001. [2] Power JD et al. PNAS 2019. [3] Andersson JLR, Sotiropoulos SN. NeuroImage
2016. [4] Fair DA et al. NeuroImage 2020.
